introduction: Hawaiʻi’s earned income tax credit is claimed on the state tax return, not through a public-assistance portal. For tax year 2025, use Form N-356 and Schedule CR with the applicable Hawaiʻi return.

sections.who: The 2025 instructions require claiming federal EITC and using the same filing status and dependents on the Hawaiʻi return. Part-year residents and nonresidents use an income-ratio adjustment. Other exclusions in the instructions can apply.
sections.get: For tax year 2025, the new refundable credit starts at 40% of the federal EITC, with the required adjustment for part-year or nonresident filers. The 2025 instructions also distinguish an older, nonrefundable 2022 carryover.

sections.apply:
1. Select the correct tax year

    Use the Department of Taxation forms directory. Do not apply 2025 instructions to a different return year without checking.

  2. Complete the credit calculation

    Follow the N-356 qualification questions and computation. A tax preparer can help distinguish a new credit from an older carryover.

  3. File the state return

    Attach the required credit forms and retain the return and submission confirmation.
sections.after: Read tax-agency requests and correct errors through the appropriate return process. The 2025 instructions state a credit-claim deadline and special rules for later IRS adjustments; consult them promptly if amending.
sections.sources: Checked October 1, 2026 using 2025 Form N-356 and instructions, Tax-year 2025 changes, State tax forms. USA Assistance background guide. Program staff determine eligibility and available assistance.

faqs: Is this a monthly cash benefit?
No. It is a credit claimed through the Hawaiʻi income-tax return.
Which forms apply to a 2025 claim?
The state instructions identify Form N-356 and Schedule CR attached to the applicable state return.
Can I reuse the 2022 carryover for future years?
The 2025 instructions say unused 2022 EITC cannot be carried into tax years beginning after December 31, 2025. Check the instructions for your return year.
